$comment: Plain words for the Results' identifiers, read by the web app (web/src/lib/plain.ts) and the desktop app (apps/marketscan/plain_words.cpp) alike, so neither shows a schema name and both say the same thing. Words only: every number shown beside them comes from the Results. tests/test_plain_words.cpp requires an entry for every gate id, warning code and sub-grade id in results.schema.json.

evidence.name: Enough trades
evidence.asks: There have to be enough trades, including some in the later test period, to judge the rule at all.

oos_benchmark.name: Held up against holding
oos_benchmark.asks: In the period not used to pick the setting, its return for the risk taken has to match simply holding.

random_timing.name: Better than random timing
random_timing.asks: Trades held for the same lengths but on random dates have to do worse almost every time.

multiple_testing.name: Not a lucky pick
multiple_testing.asks: After allowing for every setting that was tried, the result still has to be unlikely to be chance.

plateau.name: Nearby settings work too
plateau.asks: Settings next to the chosen one have to keep most of its edge, so it isn't a lone spike.

survival.name: Losses you could live through
survival.asks: The worst fall, and how often reshuffled histories wipe out most of the money, have to stay within limits.

warnings.EXERCISE_ONLY_DATA: The price data is test-grade, so treat this as a trial run of the method rather than a finding.
warnings.MOSTLY_SYNTHETIC: Most of this history is simulated rather than real prices.
warnings.NO_OUT_OF_SAMPLE: No later period was held back for testing, so the comparison with holding covers the same years the rule was judged on.
warnings.NO_SEARCH_CORRECTION: Only one setting was tested, so nothing allows for it having been chosen after seeing others.
warnings.UNCALIBRATED_CORRECTION: The allowance for trying many settings is an estimate that hasn't been calibrated yet.
warnings.FEW_TRADES_IN_SWEEP: Some settings traded too rarely to rank. They're listed, but couldn't be chosen.
warnings.OPEN_POSITION_AT_END: The rule was still holding at the end, so its last trade is valued at the final price.
warnings.SWEEP_EDGE: The chosen setting is at the edge of the range tried. A wider range might choose differently.

objectives.sortino: best return for its downside swings
objectives.calmar: best annual return for its worst drop

volatility.name: Volatility
volatility.reads: How much it swings, a year

versus_holding.name: Versus holding
versus_holding.reads: Return and worst drop against holding
